summary_en: MSE, a company majority-owned by Shobunsha Holdings' representative director Kuroda Shigeo, launched a tender offer to acquire all shares of Shobunsha Holdings (excluding treasury stock and shares held by Kuroda) at an undisclosed price, with the transaction expected to delist the company from the Tokyo Stock Exchange Standard Market.
title_en: Notice Regarding the Commencement of a Tender Offer for Shares of Shobunsha Holdings, Inc. (Securities Code: 9475) by MSE Inc.
translation_en_brief:
MSE Inc., an asset management company established in October 2023 and fully owned by Shobunsha Holdings' representative director Kuroda Shigeo and his relatives, announced the commencement of a tender offer on November 6, 2026, to acquire all shares of Shobunsha Holdings (TSE Standard Market listed, ticker 9475), excluding treasury stock and shares held by Kuroda, as part of a management buyout (MBO) transaction. The tender offer price has not been disclosed in this announcement. MSE currently holds 19.14% of Shobunsha's shares as the second-largest shareholder, while Kuroda owns 10.49% as the third-largest shareholder.

As a condition to the tender offer, Kuroda has executed a non-tendering agreement, confirming that he will not tender his shares in this offer and has committed to voting in favor of any squeeze-out procedures (本スクイーズアウト手続) at an extraordinary shareholders' meeting should the tender offer succeed. This non-tendering commitment effectively ensures that Kuroda will retain his shareholding post-transaction while facilitating the delisting of the company. Kuroda intends to remain as representative director and continue managing the company after the transaction closes.

Regarding the post-transaction management structure, the announcement states that no agreements have been reached between MSE and other current directors (including audit committee members) regarding their future roles or treatment. The composition of the board and overall management structure following successful completion of the tender offer will be determined through consultation between MSE and Shobunsha after the offer closes. The transaction is intended to result in the privatization of Shobunsha Holdings.
